newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says committed to troubled steel projects.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says committed to troubled steel projects.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Monday said it remained committed to its troubled steel mill projects which have already swallowed $8 billion for little result.

"Because the steel sector is vital for the country's industrial development, government is determined to revitalise the steel projects," finance minister Anthony Ani said during a breakdown of the 1997 fiscal budget.
Ani said 6.6 billion naira had been agreed in 1997 for the largest of the projects, the Ajaokuta steel mill.
Ajaokuta is one of four steel rolling mills ordered by a government awash with oil money in the 1970s, to reduce imports and use Nigerian iron ore.

Last week, state-run News Agency of Nigeria quoted sources at the Ajaokuta mill as saying Russia's Tiajpromexport (TPE), had been paid 50 billion naira ($625 million) at end-1996 to terminate the $5 billion contract.
The World Bank has advised the government to stop the projects saying that even if they are operational it would be cheaper to import steel than to make it in Nigeria.
